terms.gloss: represent, act for (a person, a body)
terms.grammar: phrase: persōnam with the genitive of whom one represents
evidence: Cic. Off. 1.124: intellegere sē gerere persōnam cīvitātis
terms.comment: Persōna is the actor’s mask and so the part one plays; persōnam sustinēre is the same (Cic. Pis. 24, Lewis & Short). Morgan–Owens also give vicem gerere.

terms.gloss: on behalf of, in the name of
terms.grammar: the ablative of nōmen, with a genitive or a possessive: meō, tuō nōmine
evidence: Cic. Att. 1.16.16: tuō nōmine grātiās ēgī
Cic. Att. 3.15.8: meō nōmine litterās darī

terms.gloss: not “act for”: classically, bring before the mind, show; portray; pay at once
terms.comment: Lewis & Short give “bring before one, show, exhibit”, “represent, portray” (of artists, post-Augustan) and, in trade, “pay on the spot”; never acting on someone’s behalf.

phrases.latin: Est igitur proprium mūnus magistrātūs intellegere sē gerere persōnam cīvitātis
phrases.english: It is, then, the particular duty of a magistrate to understand that he represents the state
I thanked Antonius on your behalf

phrases.latin: sī quī erunt quibus putēs opus esse meō nōmine litterās darī, velim cōnscrībās cūrēsque dandās
phrases.english: if there is anyone you think should have a letter in my name, please write it and see that it is delivered
